3.2 '538's seat p x the model's own P(decides | tie)': what conditioning on 538's mean would do
    (a) the record: the swing given the tie from the model's own mean for the seat;
    (b) the swing given the tie from 538's mean, with the model's sd_a and s_e;
    (c) 538's mean and sd as the seat's marginal: s_e,i = sqrt(sd_538^2 - sd_a^2) (as the presidency treats 538),

10.4 THE RULE AS WRITTEN (REPORT 2.6, 2.7, 0.1) AGAINST WHAT WAS APPLIED (chambers.py near_tie_test, variant_test, as backtest.json records it)
  Written: a scheme/variant is adopted only if, on the years it reaches, it (1) raises the mean log score, (2) brings the 49-51% count
  nearer the count seen, (3) moves no safe-band count further from the count seen; of those that pass, the better log score.
  Applied (reproduced above): (1) and (2) strict (>, <); (3) 'further' strict (>), so an equal distance passes; the variants'
  safe cells are tested where the count seen or none's expected is 5 or more; bands by none's mean; the near-tie test's safe
  band is 49-51% in |mean - 1/2| >= 0.10 only. Both tests pick the best log score among those that pass.
  every recorded fitting set (fit_years, k, lambda, F) holds earlier years only: yes [measured over the files and backtest.json]
  Since #51 (REPORT 0.1) a fourth condition: (4) the three hold with any one scored year left out (10.6 below).
  house: variants passing (1)-(3) none (best 'none'); passing (4) too none; the best log score among them 'none'; recorded adopted 'none' -> consistent
  senate: variants passing (1)-(3) none (best 'none'); passing (4) too none; the best log score among them 'none'; recorded adopted 'none' -> consistent
  governor: variants passing (1)-(3) ['t4', 'both'] (best 't4'); passing (4) too none; the best log score among them 'none'; recorded adopted 'none' -> consistent

39.4 The methods, each difference a reading
  1. The unit. D3's part 1 adds a state's House lines together (or reads the governor); c38 reads each federal and statewide
     contest against its own D1 or D2 record. A district short by 8% inside a state within 0.1% passes his (Washington 2022's
     eighth district, where 13 local p rest on the file) and is listed by mine.
  2. 2024. D3's gate for 2024 is the president against D1's count; c38 reads the president, the Senate, every House seat and the
     governor. North Dakota 2024's governor rows are absent in Burleigh and Divide counties (-14%) with the president whole;
     New York 2024's Monroe County lacks US House rows for 200 of 659 precincts and Assembly rows for 185 (29% of its presidential
     vote), Ontario County Assembly rows for 54 of 92 (53%), with the president and the Senate whole: the Assembly p of those
     counties rest on short counts, which the president's gate cannot see.
  3. Fusion. D3 sums a candidate's lines (Connecticut, New York) and, where D2's record holds the party line alone, compares that
     line; c38 compares the record's total and leader with the file's and lists the difference. The record's figure is the
     reading either way: Connecticut 2018's Lamont 676,649 is the Democratic line; the file's lines summed give 694,509.
  4. D2's governors. D2's total_votes is its two leading candidates' sum where its source gives no more (Rhode Island 2018,
     West Virginia 2024, Wyoming 2022, Missouri 2024, New Hampshire 2018 and 2024, Indiana 2024, North Carolina 2020); D3's
     part 1 matches the two leaders, so it sees no gap; c38 lists the totals apart from the leaders. p's n is the two-party
     n by design, so no p moves; the label does.
  5. Klarner. D3's part 2 flags a state-year where over 5% of candidates sit at 2x or 1/2 or the median is off by 3%: a test
     for doubling. c38 lists every district off by more than 5% by the two parties' lines (or every vote), on either side:
     249 districts in c38-districts.json (Idaho 2022's first Senate district filed unopposed, Vermont 2018's Chittenden at
     3.7x, Michigan 2022's 63rd House and 3rd Senate districts, New York 2022's 56th Senate district, and MEDSL's partial districts
     in the 2016 state file and the 2022 'local' files). Neither side is right by default; each is a reading for a state count.
  6. No second count. D3 lists 2020 as untested; c38 lists with it DC 2018, the odd-year legislatures of 2023 and 2025, Louisiana
     2023, North Carolina's odd years and primaries, and reads Klarner's chamber-years without a MEDSL file against the
     chamber's own history (the coarse tier), which neither check can settle without a state count.
  7. Subtotal rows. Both checks found the county-total rows (Idaho 2022, Oregon 2018, Michigan 2022) and New Jersey 2024's
     municipality rows under mode TOTAL (D3's part 3: 140 rows; c38: 1,478,257 votes over 14 federal and statewide contests,
     Bergen's fifth district at +79% raw and +0.02% once dropped), by rules written apart: D3 drops a row equal to the rest of
     its county for every candidate; c38 drops a named total equal to the county's other rows, or a row whose name the
     county's other rows extend and equal, within 0.5% or 10 votes. New Jersey 2018's Camden precincts, every one named
     '... TOTAL', are kept by both.
